newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices gain as stocks ease.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices gain as stocks ease.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday saw gains as with stocks easing on dwindling arrivals but mill buying remained slow at the higher level, dealers said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10/25 rupees at 960/1,005 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up to 1,720/1,825 rupees per maund from 1,700/1,750 rupees.
Daily arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region dropped to 500/700 bales (170 kg each). Cotton F-414 also climbed up by 5/25 rupees at 2,015/2,035 rupees per maund.
"Arrivals in the Gujarat region are also coming down and prices of the Gujarat varieties remained firm," one broker said.

In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan rose by 300 rupees at 14,500/15,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton rose by 100 rupees at 13,200 rupees and Kala-ginned rose by 100 rupees at 12,700 rupees per candy.
